subject: Priority Sentinel: PayNest throughput regressions & exec alignment
messages:
From: Ethan Sanders <ethan.sanders@paynest.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: PayNest Ops <oncall@paynest.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + 500s impacting checkout (urgent)

Dylan —

We started seeing a sharp throughput drop across our API surface around 08:45 PT. Checkout calls are spiking 500s (roughly 2–3% of requests) and median latency has blown up for smaller payloads. Our customers are seeing timeouts. Our ops team collected traces and a sample log file (attached).

Can you confirm this is on your side or if something in our integration changed? We need an ETA on resolution — this is impacting live transactions.

Attaching: paynest-sample-logs.txt (text)

— Ethan
Head of Engineering, PayNest

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Sanders <ethan.sanders@paynest.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 500s impacting checkout (urgent)

Ethan — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. We’ve started a triage and I’ve looped in infra (Aditya) and your CSM (Ben).

Initial checks: no global deploys from our side in the last 24 hours. We’ve opened a ticket (PS-1207) and enabled detailed request tracing for your account. Can you confirm the region these requests were hitting? We’ll also need a short-term mitigation plan.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Enable verbose tracing and preserve samples for 2 hours
- Re-route a subset of traffic to warm standby nodes
- If error rate doesn’t drop in 30m, we’ll roll back last quantized kernel and increase dedicated pool by 2 nodes (temporary)

We’ll stand up a war-room tomorrow at 09:00 PT to brief leadership and coordinate next steps. I’ll send dial-in and agenda shortly.

— Dylan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 07:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 500s impacting checkout (urgent)

Quick telemetry readout from the PayNest trace bucket (attached snapshot):
- p95 and p99 show a bimodal shift concurrent with a rise in small-batch requests from a particular client region (us-west-2).
- KV cache eviction rates spiked; prefix cache hits dropped by ~35% between 08:40–09:05 PT.
- We’ve seen similar signatures before when kernel quantization changed memory access patterns for KV cache.

Suggested mitigations to try before capacity changes:
1) Temporarily disable the recent quantized kernel for your model variant (rollback to vQ0).
2) Re-enable aggressive prefix caching for PayNest routes and pin a conservative max-batch size.

I’ve attached a quick snapshot (telemetry-snapshot-0702.png). If the rollback doesn’t reduce 5xx within 20–30m, Aditya — please proceed with capacity bump.

— Laura
Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry-snapshot-0702.png (image)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Sanders <ethan.sanders@paynest.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: customer comm for PayNest (review)

Ethan —

We’re drafting a short customer-facing update for your team and key stakeholders. Proposed text below — please poke holes: 

"PayNest team — we identified elevated error rates and increased latency tied to a recent inference kernel change and caching behavior. Our engineers are rolling back the kernel for your routes and applying temporary caching rules. We expect reduced errors within 30 minutes and will provide a full timeline and remediation summary shortly. A war-room is scheduled for 09:00 PT to coordinate final actions. — Redwood Inference Ops"

Ben here — pushing for transparency but we also want to avoid premature technical detail in the broader customer comms. Executives may want an optioned message (consumer-facing vs. partner ops). Laura — is the rollback safe to call out? Aditya — do we have an ETA for the capacity bump if needed?

— Ben
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Infra update: tests, short-term mitigations, and recommended capacity change

Team — summary of what we ran and what I’m seeing:
- Commanded rollback of quantized kernel for PayNest model variant at 08:50 PT (rollback-id: rb-707).
- Reconfigured prefix caching thresholds and set max-batch-size to conservative value for routes: paynest-checkout, paynest-session.
- Enabled reroute to warm-standby pool for 15% of traffic.

Results after mitigation (08:50–09:10):
- 5xx rate dropped from ~2.7% to ~0.8% on sampled traffic
- Median latency moved from 820ms -> 220ms for affected payloads

If metrics hold for the next 30m, we can avoid an immediate capacity increase. But if there is rebound, I recommend increasing dedicated pool by +2 nodes (estimated lead time ~18m to provision warm nodes and drain safely). I’ve started the capacity proposal doc and attached a short PDF.

Links: time-series (internal) | Jira PS-1207 | PagerDuty INC-89214

— Aditya
VP, Infrastructure

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai

- Quick timeline + current metrics (Laura)
- What we ran and immediate impact (Aditya)

Dial-in: zoom.redwood/warroom-paynest (passcode on calendar)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Sanders <ethan.sanders@paynest.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 18:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: PayNest throughput normalized, next steps, and customer credit proposal

Ethan —

Quick post-incident summary and next steps following today’s war-room: 

What happened (brief):
- Starting 2028-07-01 08:45 PT we observed a throughput regression and elevated 5xx driven by a recent quantized kernel interacting poorly with KV cache behavior for specific batch patterns.

Immediate remediation and impact:
- We rolled back the quantized kernel for PayNest routes (rb-707) and adjusted prefix caching + batch sizing.
- We routed 15% of traffic to warm-standby and observed 5xx drop from ~2.7% -> 0.6% within 20 minutes. Median latency returned to baseline (~210ms).
- No data integrity issues were observed.

Customer-facing ask / offer:
- We recommend a 3-day monitoring window with enhanced telemetry and weekly syncs.
- Redwood proposes a one-time credits package to make up for measured lost transactions during the incident window; Ben will follow up with numbers and a formal credit note.

Next steps (owners):
- Aditya: finalize capacity proposal and postmortem (ETA: 2028-07-06) — attachment: capacity-increase-proposal.pdf
- Laura: produce technical postmortem draft for internal review (attached: postmortem-draft-v1.md)
- Ben: finalize customer-facing comm and credit statement (tomorrow EOD)
- Dylan: exec readout prep for CEO at 15:00 PT (slides attached in shared drive)

Attachments: postmortem-draft-v1.md (text), capacity-increase-proposal.pdf (pdf)

We’ll keep the war-room open for 24 hours of monitoring. If you’d like immediate access to traces or a dedicated technical bridge, ping this thread and we’ll open a direct channel.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the formal postmortem and the credit proposal.

— Dylan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142
